doc.title: Etta Jones interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 2, 1998

title: Sidemen on the record and tenor players she worked with
summary: Frank Wess, Roy Haynes and George Duvivier played on the album; she names tenor players such as Gene Ammons, Sonny Stitt and Illinois Jacquet.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: And you get to associate, I mean on that particular record, you had Frank Wess and Roy Haynes.
I had George Duvivier on bass on that.
Wow. And you’ve worked with a lot of good tenor players too, starting, well maybe not starting with Houston but—

With Gene Ammons, with Sonny Stitt, alto and tenor, with what’s his name — let’s see I’m going to get a blank now — Illinois, I worked with Illinois Jacquet. I’ve worked with — I can’t think, I’m getting a blank — but wonderful tenor players.
